name: Energetic Flyby
description: A continuous flight down a twisting tunnel of glassy, perforated shells lit from inside, following a spiked, spinning sphere cluster that throws light rods through the tunnel. Kali's Energetic Flyby (Shadertoy csjGDD, CC BY-NC-SA 3.0), its march cut for cost and run at native resolution. Each downbeat on the cached grid (barPhase01) turns the glow's colour, pink to orange to pink to blue; every second downbeat banks the camera a quarter turn. The song's energy (spectralFlux, self-normalised) sets the flight speed and the glow level; the bass (bassDev, self-normalised) spins the spheres.
author: Kali (port: Uzume engine)

audio_routes.note: EFB.1 - each wrap of the cached grid's barPhase01 is a downbeat: the glow colour steps 0.7 rad along pink -> orange -> pink -> blue (inside Kali's range), eased 0.25 s; every second downbeat banks the camera a quarter turn over 1 s. No brightness flare: at Kali's glow any flare took the worst-case flash train over the regional limit (Matt's call). EnergeticFlybyState.

EFB.1 — spectralFlux self-normalised against its own running mean (8 s warm-up rule, FH.17), smoothed 0.6 s: flight speed 0.65 + 0.8 x energy and glow 0.9 + 0.7 x energy (a typical passage = Kali's average glow, 1.25).
EFB.1 — positive bassDev self-normalised the same way, attack 30 ms / release 300 ms: sphere spin rate 1 + 3 x bass.
